trials.role: Intravenous Iproplatin (CHIP) monotherapy: phase I pharmacokinetics
trials.outcome: Plasma pharmacokinetics were evaluated in 12 patients and urinary Pt recovery in 19. The investigators cite the parent phase I programme MTD of 350 mg/m² every 3–4 weeks and report myelosuppression as dose limiting. No clear association between the measured PK parameters and toxicity was demonstrated in this substudy.

toxicity.Notes: Table 1: LD50 54 mg/kg in mice bearing the parent ADJ/PC6 plasmacytoma (ED90 4 mg/kg, therapeutic index 14), single i.p. dose on day 20, three animals per dose, LD50 by the method of Weil; in the cisplatin-resistant sublines the LD50 was 76 and 90 mg/kg

Table II: LD50 90 mg/kg, ID90 7.5 mg/kg, therapeutic index 12 in female BALB/c mice bearing the ADJ/PC6A plasmacytoma (method as in earlier work of the group; route and schedule not restated); cisplatin: LD50 13, ID90 1.6, TI 8.1

pk.Dosing: 30-minute IV infusion, varied renal function, overall cohort
pk.Notes: Pendyala et al. (1985), abstract. Across patients with varying renal function, median terminal t½ 3.16 h (reported SD 2.6 h). Mean total body clearance 14.25 ± 3.99 L/h and mean steady-state volume Vss 39.9 ± 25.0 L. Clearance correlated with creatinine clearance. Numeric dose levels and number of subjects are unavailable in the abstract.

pk.Dosing: Early Phase I programme, 20–350 mg/m² every 3–4 weeks
pk.Notes: Creaven, Pendyala and Madajewicz, abstract (1986), investigator summary of their clinical pharmacokinetic studies. See the related original 12-patient dataset in Pendyala et al. 1983 (DOI 10.1007/BF00257411). The abstract of that original paper reports ranges across dose levels. Individual results and number contributing to the summary estimate are unavailable. Approximate half-life for unchanged CHIP. The related 1983 abstract reports 0.64–1.27 h. The 1983 study used HPLC separation and atomic absorption for the parent drug.

pk.Dosing: Early Phase I programme, 20–350 mg/m² every 3–4 weeks
pk.Notes: Creaven, Pendyala and Madajewicz, abstract (1986), investigator summary of their clinical pharmacokinetic studies. See the related original 12-patient dataset in Pendyala et al. 1983 (DOI 10.1007/BF00257411). The abstract of that original paper reports ranges across dose levels. Individual results and number contributing to the summary estimate are unavailable. The value is the terminal beta phase, with a reported range of 32.1–124 h in the related 1983 abstract. Filterable Pt was measured separately; the 1983 abstract reports a terminal range of 17.8–54.6 h at higher doses.

pk.Dosing: Single IV dose in 0.9% saline, adult 9–12 kg dogs
pk.Notes: Pendyala, Cowens and Creaven, 1982, Methods and Results pp. 510–513, Fig. 2 and discussion. Total plasma Pt measured by flameless atomic absorption. Terminal beta t½ 39.4 ± 4.6 h and initial alpha t½ 0.6 ± 0.1 h. The authors separately estimated the apparent plasma t½ of unchanged CHIP at 0.3–0.5 h from urinary excretion rates by TLC/HPLC. That is a range derived from urine, rather than a directly measured plasma value. Urinary recovery of total Pt at 24 h was 45–72% in five dogs.
